ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Rectangle $R_0$ has sides of lengths $3$ and $4$. Rectangles $R_1$, $R_2$, and $R_3$ are formed such that:
$\bullet$ all four rectangles share a common vertex $P$,
$\bullet$ for each $n = 1, 2, 3$, one side of $R_n$ is a diagonal of $R_{n-1}$,
$\bullet$ for each $n = 1, 2, 3$, the opposite side of $R_n$ passes through a vertex of $R_{n-1}$ such that the center of $R_n$ is located counterclockwise of the center of $R_{n-1}$ with respect to $P$.
Compute the total area covered by the union of the four rectangles.
<image1>

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the four rectangles all share the common bottom vertex P, and unfold in a counterclockwise fan shape. R0 is the rectangle to the right; R1, R2, R3 successively use the diagonal of the previous rectangle starting from P as one side, and are placed on the side more counterclockwise relative to P. The figure also shows that, each time a new rectangle is added, its overlap with the already covered part is the half region into which the previous rectangle is divided by that diagonal. Reasoning: The side lengths of R0 are 3 and 4, so area(R0)=3×4=12. Suppose that when going from R_{n-1} to R_n, the length of the diagonal used is d, and the perpendicular distance from the corresponding vertex in the previous rectangle to this diagonal is h. This diagonal divides R_{n-1} into two equal-area triangles, therefore area(R_{n-1})=d h. One side length of R_n is also d, and the width in the other direction is exactly h, so area(R_n)=d h=area(R_{n-1}). Therefore the areas of the four rectangles are all 12. From the counterclockwise arrangement in the figure, each new rectangle R1, R2, R3 overlaps half of the previous rectangle with the already covered region, with area 6, so each new rectangle only adds an area of 12−6=6. The total covered area is 12+6+6+6=30.

method.method_draft: First read the image to determine the outer boundary order of the union: starting at P, follow the bottom/right side of R0, then the successive far vertices of R0, R1, R2, R3, then the remaining counterclockwise side vertex of R3, and return to P. Set P as the origin. Let rectangle R_k have adjacent side vectors a_k and b_k from P, with vertices 0, a_k, b_k, a_k+b_k, oriented as in the image. For R0 choose vectors of lengths 4 and 3, so det(a_0,b_0)=12. The construction gives a_{k+1}=a_k+b_k, because this is the diagonal of R_k used as a side of R_{k+1}. Also, since the opposite side of R_{k+1} passes through the b_k-vertex of R_k, the vector b_k-b_{k+1} is parallel to a_{k+1}; hence det(a_{k+1},b_{k+1})=det(a_{k+1},b_k)=det(a_k+b_k,b_k)=det(a_k,b_k)=12. Thus every determinant det(a_k,b_k) is 12. From the image, the union boundary polygon is 0, a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4, b_3. Apply the shoelace formula: area = 1/2[det(a_0,a_1)+det(a_1,a_2)+det(a_2,a_3)+det(a_3,a_4)+det(a_4,b_3)]. Each of the first four determinants equals 12, and det(a_4,b_3)=det(a_3+b_3,b_3)=det(a_3,b_3)=12. Therefore the area is 1/2·5·12=30.

图像描述：图中四个矩形都从同一个底部公共点 P 出发。R0 在右下方，底边从 P 向右，右边竖直向上；R1 以 R0 的对角线作为一条边并向逆时针方向扩展；R2、R3 继续按同样方式向左上方绕 P 逆时针展开。根据图中外轮廓，从 P 出发沿 R0 的底边到右下顶点，再依次经过 R0、R1、R2、R3 的远端顶点，最后到 R3 的另一侧顶点，再回到 P。因此外边界可按 0, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, b3 的顺序表示。

推理：令 P 为原点。设矩形 R_k 从 P 出发的两条邻边向量为 a_k 和 b_k，则其四个顶点为 0, a_k, b_k, a_k+b_k。对 R0，边长为 3 和 4，所以 det(a0,b0)=12。

由构造，R_{k+1} 的一条边是 R_k 的对角线，所以 a_{k+1}=a_k+b_k。又因为 R_{k+1} 的对边经过 R_k 的 b_k 顶点，该对边与 a_{k+1} 平行，所以 b_k-b_{k+1} 与 a_{k+1} 平行。因此 det(a_{k+1},b_{k+1})=det(a_{k+1},b_k)=det(a_k+b_k,b_k)=det(a_k,b_k)。由 det(a0,b0)=12 归纳得到每个 det(a_k,b_k)=12。

根据图中外边界多边形 0, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, b3，用鞋带公式：面积 = 1/2 [det(a0,a1)+det(a1,a2)+det(a2,a3)+det(a3,a4)+det(a4,b3)]。因为 a_{i+1}=a_i+b_i，所以前四个行列式都等于 det(a_i,b_i)=12。并且 a4=a3+b3，所以 det(a4,b3)=det(a3+b3,b3)=det(a3,b3)=12。因此总面积 = 1/2 * 5 * 12 = 30。

根据图中外边界多边形 0, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, b3，用鞋带公式：面积 = 1/2 [det(a0,a1)+det(a1,a2)+det(a2,a3)+det(a3,a4)+det(a4,b3)]。因为 a_{i+1}=a_i+b_i，所以前四个行列式都等于 det(a_i,b_i)=12。并且 a4=a3+b3，所以 det(a4,b3)=det(a3+b3,b3)=det(a3,b3)=12。因此总面积 = 1/2 * 5 * 12 = 30。

Rectangle $R_0$ has sides of lengths $3$ and $4$. Rectangles $R_1$, $R_2$, and $R_3$ are formed such that:
$\bullet$ all four rectangles share a common vertex $P$,
$\bullet$ for each $n = 1, 2, 3$, one side of $R_n$ is a diagonal of $R_{n-1}$,
$\bullet$ for each $n = 1, 2, 3$, the opposite side of $R_n$ passes through a vertex of $R_{n-1}$ such that the center of $R_n$ is located counterclockwise of the center of $R_{n-1}$ with respect to $P$.
Compute the total area covered by the union of the four rectangles.

raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the four rectangles all share the common bottom vertex P, and unfold in a counterclockwise fan shape. R0 is the rectangle to the right; R1, R2, R3 successively use the diagonal of the previous rectangle starting from P as one side, and are placed on the side more counterclockwise relative to P. The figure also shows that, each time a new rectangle is added, its overlap with the already covered part is the half region into which the previous rectangle is divided by that diagonal.

Reasoning: The side lengths of R0 are 3 and 4, so area(R0)=3×4=12. Suppose that when going from R_{n-1} to R_n, the length of the diagonal used is d, and the perpendicular distance from the corresponding vertex in the previous rectangle to this diagonal is h. This diagonal divides R_{n-1} into two equal-area triangles, therefore area(R_{n-1})=d h. One side length of R_n is also d, and the width in the other direction is exactly h, so area(R_n)=d h=area(R_{n-1}). Therefore the areas of the four rectangles are all 12. From the counterclockwise arrangement in the figure, each new rectangle R1, R2, R3 overlaps half of the previous rectangle with the already covered region, with area 6, so each new rectangle only adds an area of 12−6=6. The total covered area is 12+6+6+6=30.
